title: August 2026 fresh-intake production - batch H2 (four verified-current regulatory asks: SIRE 2.0, the latest Grain Code amendment, the National Shipping Board, and India's maritime climate initiatives)
note: FOUR ROOTS, FOUR NEW CARDS, ONE PER ASK. Three of the four sat in lane Q-C, the currentness-sensitive lane, and that judgement paid: in each of them the position established from the issuer's own most recent publication differed from, or went beyond, the earlier programme-by-programme currency record. WHY EACH IS A NEW CARD AND NOT AN EXPANSION. SIRE 2.0 (AUG-0114, with limbs AUG-0115 'who carries it out' and AUG-0116 'why is it required'): a word-boundary search for SIRE returned no card on the subject; the nearest card, QB9_F#q9 RightShip Inspection, states in terms that SIRE dominates the tanker sector, so the new card is that card's sibling and belongs in the same file. Grain Code amendment (AUG-0147): QB2_A#q11 already teaches Grain Code stability, but the ask is a currency question about an amendment and would be buried inside a long stability card; q11 is instead CORRECTED, separately, to stop presenting the pre-2026 two-configuration model as complete. National Shipping Board (AUG-0119): no card on the subject; QB1_F#q12 mentions the MS Act only for seafarer welfare. Indian climate initiatives (AUG-0123): QB10_A#q5 covers Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 and the new card cross-refers to it rather than restating it - the ask is about the CURRENT initiative set, whose policy layer did not exist when q5 was written. SOURCE WORK, WHICH IS MOST OF THIS BATCH. Primary sources were obtained and preserved for three of the four: resolution MSC.552(108) itself from IMO's resolutions index - obtained after review, when the January 2026 publication supplement the batch first relied on turned out to OMIT annex item 6 and to carry no operative clauses at all, so the supplement alone could not establish that the amendment binds existing ships; the Gazette of India notification G.S.R. 379(E) of 20 May 2026 and section 4 of the Merchant Shipping Act 2025, both from DGMA's own portal; and DGMA's draft National Maritime Decarbonisation Policy Framework of 3 July 2026. The fourth, SIRE 2.0, is PARTIALLY primary: OCIMF's own programme page carries the architecture, the CVIQ, the three assessment elements and the inspector and submitting-company structure, but its go-live date sits in an image-only press release and its FAQ behind an expired signed link. Neither was worked around, and the card's source-confidence line says which half is which. EXAMINER ATTRIBUTION. All four asks are PANEL_LEVEL_ONLY. No examiner name was added to any card or to the cheat sheet; relationships stay at 958 and examiners at 7. INDEPENDENT REVIEW AND WHAT IT CHANGED. A clean-context reviewer, given the governed questions, the card text and the primary sources and barred from the producing reasoning, returned: QB2_A#q33 ACCEPTED, QB9_F#q12 ACCEPTED_WITH_BOUNDED_FIX, QB1_F#q21 REVISE, QB10_A#q7 REVISE. Four blocking findings, all confirmed by the producer against the primary sources before any fix was applied, and all bounded within their own card. (1) QB10_A#q7 named JNPT and Kochi as the Green Tug Transition Programme pilot ports. The framework's NARRATIVE chapter says that; its DEPLOYMENT-STATUS chapter says Phase 1 is Deendayal, JNPA, Paradip and V.O. Chidambaranar, with Cochin waiting until its diesel tug contract expires in August 2027. The card had also told a Kochi MMD candidate to volunteer 'Kochi as a GTTP pilot port' as one of three hard numbers - the one fact a local panel would be most likely to know is false. Corrected in the 60-second answer, the body, the REG-BOX, the CE Oral Tip and the inline cheat sheet. (2) QB10_A#q7 flatly denied that any port version of the CII exists; the same framework names a Port Carbon Intensity Indicator and says Harit Sagar reporting is aligned to it. The real distinction is kept, the denial removed. (3) QB1_F#q21 gave the March 2026 NSB meeting as the latest verified; DGMA had already published the 16-17 April 2026 Mumbai meeting - on a card whose entire lesson is not being stale. (4) QB1_F#q21 said the Board meets quarterly; that is the Rules' norm, and this Board has met roughly monthly, which is what made the stale answer look one meeting behind instead of four. Retrieving the April minutes also produced a better finding than the review had: BOTH the March and April minutes call themselves the '31st meeting', so the ordinal is unusable, and the April set confirms 10 March 2026 as the date the March set contradicted itself about. The card now gives dates and venues and no ordinals. Non-blocking findings taken: OCIMF's own page names four question types including CONDITIONAL and defines Performance Influencing Factors, both of which the card and the registry had under-credited as secondary; the Cabinet allocation of Rs 69,725 crore and the framework's own admission that none of it is green-conditioned; the 15.48% renewable baseline behind the 60% target; the proposed 2027 coastal biofuel blending mandate; and a trim of every 15-second answer, which ran 81 to 116 words against a corpus median of 67. One reviewer suggestion was DECLINED: quoting roughly 100 questions per SIRE inspection. OCIMF publishes no count and says only that the compiled questionnaire reduces the number assigned, so importing a trade-press figure into a card whose virtue is source discipline would have been the wrong trade. ---- COMPANION CORRECTION ---- CORR-GRAIN-MSC552-20260831 (tools/oral/correction_corr_grain_msc552_20260831_manifest.json) corrects QB2_A#q11, which already existed. This batch authorises only the cards that did not. ---- KNOWN TRAPS ---- Entry 55 added to meoclass1/known_traps.md, covering the Grain Code's third loading configuration. ---- REVISION LAYER ---- QB9_F_CheatSheet.html: UPDATED IN THIS BATCH. Its flip-cards are one-per-question and were exactly 1:1 with the file's eleven questions, so a twelfth question with no flip-card would have left a visibly incomplete revision surface. A Q12 flip-card carrying the 15-second answer and a Rapid-Recall Index row were added by hand; there is no generator for this file. The index's examiner column is an em dash on purpose - AUG-0114 is PANEL_LEVEL_ONLY, and writing a name into a harvestable surface would manufacture an examiner relationship. Re-synced after review: the Q12 flip-card carries the 15-second answer verbatim, so trimming that answer required the flip-card to be rewritten with it. A revision surface that quietly keeps the old wording is worse than one that is missing. QB10_A.html: UPDATED IN THIS BATCH. This file's revision layer is an INLINE cheat sheet at the foot of the page, not a separate file. A cue-card and a Rapid-Reference table row were added for the new question. Both the cue-card and the table row carried the GTTP pilot-port error and were corrected with the card - the reason the revision layer has to be treated as part of the card, not as an afterthought. QB2_A_CheatSheet.html: NOT UPDATED - and this is a judgement, not an omission. It is a sixteen-page curated concept sheet (risk universe, flowcharts, comparison matrices), not a per-question index: it carries 22 question references against 32 questions, so a new card does not automatically earn a page. It was also checked for exposure to the amendment and contains NO filled / partly-filled enumeration, so MSC.552(108) does not make anything on it wrong. Its Grain content is the three intact-stability criteria and the Document of Authorisation, both unchanged by the amendment. QB1_FG_CheatSheet.html: NOT UPDATED. A curated cue-card sheet spanning QB1_F and QB1_G with no per-question index and no existing National Shipping Board content. Recorded as an H5 consideration rather than hand-extended here. ---- CORPUS WORK ---- shared_desktop_corpus: F:/RulesApp-Local-Input/true-source - updated under the Founder authorisation for MIW to update a verified affected IMO instrument. NEW instrument area 03-imo-instruments/Grain-Code/ with INSTRUMENT_LOG.md, manifest.json and IMO's own January 2026 supplement; the central 10-amendment-register updated in both .json and .md; 01-source-inventory/SOURCE_REGISTER.json and .csv refreshed; RQ-G01 and RQ-G02 added to 99-review-queue. In 06-india-law-and-dg-shipping/Merchant-Shipping-Act-2025/ the NSB Rules 2026 gazette was filed under _rules/ and the instrument log extended - RQ-32 CLOSED because the held base PDF proved byte-identical to DGMA's own published copy, so its rank rose from secondary mirror to authority-hosted without the bytes changing, and RQ-33 left open. No unrelated instrument was touched and no superseded history was removed. miw_knowledge_central: Knowledge Central/india-maritime-decarbonisation/ and Knowledge Central/national-shipping-board/ hold the DGMA draft framework and the NSB minutes. Git-ignored, as that corpus already is. registry: docs/sources/MIW_SOURCE_REGISTRY.json gains SRC-GRAINCODE-MSC552-2026, SRC-NSBRULES-2026, SRC-MSACT-2025, SRC-NSB-MIN31-2026, SRC-NMDPF-2026 and SRC-OCIMF-SIRE20. Each carries its currentness state, how it was checked, its revalidation trigger, and an explicit claims_NOT_established list. ---- INDEPENDENT REVIEW, STRUCTURED RECORD ---- method: clean-context subagent, given the governed questions, the card text, the local primary sources and the web, and barred from the producing reasoning; verdicts: QB2_A.html#q33 = ACCEPTED; QB9_F.html#q12 = ACCEPTED_WITH_BOUNDED_FIX; QB1_F.html#q21 = REVISE - fixed, bounded; QB10_A.html#q7 = REVISE - fixed, bounded; QB2_A.html#q11 = ACCEPTED; blocking findings: 4, all fixed: True; every finding was re-verified by the producer against the primary source before any fix was applied. A finding the review did not have: Retrieving the April 2026 NSB minutes showed that BOTH the March and the April sets are titled the '31st meeting'. The reviewer had called the later one the 32nd, from DGMA's listing rather than the document. The card now quotes no ordinal at all. A suggestion declined: A question count for SIRE 2.0. OCIMF publishes none; the card says so instead. ---- SCHEMA NOTE ---- companion_correction, corpus_work, independent_review, revision_layer and known_traps_entries are not in the batch schema's closed field set, so they are folded into this note rather than carried as fields no gate can read. That closed set is deliberate: a field no validator touches is decoration, and decoration is how a record starts looking more authoritative than it is.
